scope: Constructed short ENOSPC fault, not a live official capture or host disk exhaustion
input: A fresh separately mounted 4–64 MiB disposable filesystem; working state and evidence must be on another filesystem
fault: After readiness and an acknowledged Unicode document write, fill only an exclusive synthetic file on the tiny export filesystem until the OS returns ENOSPC
criteria: Actual filler write receives ENOSPC and available export space is recorded
Native export fails with the OS no-space error and nonzero process exit
Functions orderly teardown completes; all owned ports close; Hub locator is removed
No completed portable export is published; partial-path evidence is retained
Native receipt and acknowledged write survive same-directory reopen
Recovery export to the unaffected evidence filesystem completes
limitations: Does not establish behavior when the native working-data disk itself fills, during host power loss, or when an entire machine runs out of memory. No pre-existing volume is formatted or filled.
